edge.title: The QR you scan to get paid
edge.setup: You're selling something online. The buyer says his app is acting up, so he sends a QR code or a payment request and tells you to scan it or approve it so the money lands. A few taps and a PIN later, your balance is lower, not higher.
edge.tell: You were asked for your UPI PIN to receive money.
move: Receiving money never needs your PIN. A PIN screen means money is leaving your account.
Read the screen before you type anything. If it says Pay, or shows an amount you are about to send, close it.
Offer your own QR or UPI ID and let the buyer pay you. A genuine buyer will.
If money has gone, call your bank immediately and report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in the same day.
edge.why: UPI lets only the payer authorise a payment, with a PIN. Any step that asks the receiver for a PIN is the payer step in disguise. The con works by relabelling the direction of money, and the PIN is the one thing that cannot be faked.
edge.variants: Same shape: 'refund' links that ask for a PIN, collect requests labelled cashback, QR codes pasted on parcels or posters.

lens.name: Sunk cost
lens.one_line: Money and time already spent are gone, and should carry zero weight in what you do next.
lens.detail: Rationally, only future costs and benefits matter. Psychologically, abandoning something feels like converting an investment into a loss, so people escalate — another year in the wrong job, another ₹50,000 into a failing car, another two hours of a bad film. The trick that works: ask what you'd advise someone who'd just arrived at this exact situation with no history.
elsewhere: Government projects continued because of money already spent.
Relationships extended by their length rather than their state.
Reading a book to the end because you're halfway.
lens.test: If I were arriving at this fresh today, with nothing already invested, would I choose it?
lens.today: BMTC has proposed five feeder routes for the Pink Line, and the Metro safety inspector has begun inspecting the line. If you have settled into driving the same route for years, the bike EMI, the parking spot and the habit are already spent. Judge the new option on today's door-to-door time and cost, not on what you have already put into the old one.

moved.what: BMTC has proposed five feeder bus routes for the Pink Line stations, and the Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety has begun its safety inspection of the line (The Hindu, Times of India).
moved.so_what: The inspection is the step before opening, but no opening date was reported. Do not change your commute yet. Look for the final feeder route list, since that decides whether the last mile works for you.

moved.what: BMTC is moving to open its live bus data for third-party journey planning (Times of India).
moved.so_what: If it goes ahead, real-time bus arrivals could appear in the apps you already use, which makes bus-plus-Metro a more dependable fallback on bad traffic days. It is a proposal for now, so nothing to do yet.

moved.what: Bengaluru North Corporation has set up a Tuesday helpline for garbage grievances (Times of India).
moved.so_what: Tomorrow is Tuesday. If you have an uncollected-waste complaint pending, note that day and call then rather than waiting for a general line to pick up.

moved.what: Times of India reports a 'super El Niño' threatens India's coffee harvest, with Karnataka facing a 15 to 20% output slump.
moved.so_what: Expect upward pressure on coffee prices over the coming months, filter coffee powder included. Not a reason to stock up, just not to be surprised by the next price revision.

carry_over.prompt: A buyer holds up a UPI success screen and is already walking away with your phone, saying the bank server is slow. What counts as proof that you have been paid?
carry_over.answer: Confirmation came from their screen, not from your bank.
